concept.title: Do the categories meet real needs?
concept.shortdesc: The draft taxonomy is judged by whether people can find what they need with it, so each need links to the categories that should answer it.

conbody.note: The catalogue of 36 needs is a model-written draft built from the persona use cases. It has not been agreed with stakeholders. Thresholds and category links are proposals.
conbody.p: In this study the granularity of the classification is decided by what people need, not by how big a cluster happens to be. A need is a task a person is trying to do, with the words they use for it and what a good result looks like. Each need names the categories that should answer it. That makes the classification testable: for each need, in each place, can a person find a suitable service? reports a first run.

section.title: Safety needs (3)
section.p: Safety: a miss could leave someone at risk, so the bar is highest.

section.title: Important needs (19)
section.p: Important: a miss leaves someone without help they need.

section.title: Convenience needs (14)
section.p: Convenience: a miss is an inconvenience, so the bar is lower.

section.title: Needs no category answers yet
section.p: These are a finding: the discovered categories do not cover them.
